Game that will make you die many times, but that is also what makes it so enjoyable. Every death teaches you something new about the enemies, bosses, or your own playstyle. When you finally defeat a boss after many attempts, the feeling of victory is incredibly satisfying.

The world is huge, beautiful, and full of secrets. You can explore mysterious castles, dangerous caves, hidden areas, and many different locations without always knowing what you will find. There are also many weapons, spells, armor sets, and character builds, so you can choose a playstyle that suits you.

At first, the game may feel frustrating, especially for new players, but it becomes more rewarding as you improve. Elden Ring is challenging, exciting, and unforgettable. It may make you angry sometimes, but you will probably keep coming back for another try.

I highly recommend this game to anyone who enjoys exploration, difficult combat, and the satisfaction of overcoming powerful enemies.

With roughly 600-700 hours between PC and Console, I can safely say this is in my top 3 favorite games of all time. 

I came into this with the knowledge that it somehow beat the juggernaut that was God of War: Ragnarok, the follow up to the game that introduced me to single player games. This was one of the few games I've experienced where it surpassed all my expectations for it and easily cleared the very high bar.

That said, the game is not perfect. No game is, of course, but for Elden Ring, despite being the best souls game to get introduced to the series, there are many issues that much be made aware of to others before deciding on whether to purchase.


The game, while can easily run on most systems, is not the most stable fps all the time. It's not that bad for the most part, but every once in a while it can get you.

The game features a lot of stuff to do, and while most of it can be figured out by the average player, one thing that is held back are the quests. Don't get me wrong, some of them are amazing, but figuring out what to do for each can be a pain sometimes, and even worse if you aren't using guides. While I usually don't recommend them for new players, if you plan to do some quests I heavily recommend using them for convenience unless you're very good at details.

Lastly, the game is, of course, a soulsborne/like game. The gameplay will be very hit or miss. Adding onto that, not surprisingly, the game is hard. With no difficulty setting (not including in-game builds), there will be some who just won't be up for it, and that's ok. The game offers a lot of choices on your character. But still, for some they just won't get into it. For some, they don't want a game that will make them rage, or overcome great obstacles. Some just want something slower and more calm, which if this is the case then I'm not sure why you'd consider a souls game, but maybe for some they still will.


There are more issues, but these 3 are the big ones. All the other ones, in my opinion, aren't as major and are a lot more minor.

Of course, with how much praise this game gets, it has to be good, right?

Yep.

It's a masterpiece.


While the game's graphics aren't next level or anything, the art and world direction certainly are. The world not only is incredible beautiful, but it's also packed with content. Having Torrent as a steed helps with travel. There are so many areas where I can see people randomly stepping into, finding a really cool item, and then deciding to dedicate their entire run towards that.

Building off of that, the build variety is mind blowing. Items found at the very beginning can be used until the endgame. Of course, there are some stronger and weaker than others, but just about every weapon is viable. With a large selection of armor and talismans, it's hard not to find a build that you find incredibly fun.

Of course, a Fromsoft game must have bosses, and boy do they come swinging here. Not only does it feature some of the hardest bosses in the series, but also some of the overall best. I won't spoil which ones, but even the worst ones I can usually find something good going for them.

The music is, of course, a banger. No explanation needed.

Lastly is the DLC: Shadow of the Erdtree. This could be it's own review, but to put it simply I would say if you really enjoy Elden Ring, then the DLC will be worth it for you. Yeah, $40 USD is a lot for a DLC, but the sheer size of it makes it feel like a completely new game. I recommend checking out some trusted source's full, spoiler free review on it.


If you decide this is for you, then I would say there are 3 things to know going in:

1. Yes, the game is hard. But don't feel forced to go places or do certain things if they get too tedious. The world is incredibly big and open, with so many opportunities for adventure. Go out and explore.

2. With the exception (IMO) being quests, this game will generally be better received if you don't use the internet. Try to pay attention to the lines given to you in game, such as item lore, NPC dialogue, and so on. The game doesn't hold your hand on lore and story (sometimes it does though, fortunately for the important stuff).

3. While I did just list off the things I'd recommend people do for this game, at the end of the day it is just a recommendation. Play the game how you see fit, the one that helps you achieve what you set out to do. Getting frustrated on a boss and don't care how they die? Youtube search builds to your hearts content. There will be people who will try to get on your case due to how you play, but don't let that sour your experience or stop it outright.


I don't believe in perfect games, nor will there ever be one. But this is one of the few games to make me seriously question that notion


TLDR; 10/10 game

Elden Ring is the ultimate evolution of the Souls formula.

FromSoftware took everything that made Dark Souls special — challenging combat, cryptic storytelling, incredible boss design, and rewarding exploration — and expanded it into a massive open world without losing its identity.

The biggest achievement is the freedom it gives to the player. You are no longer forced into a specific path: if an obstacle feels impossible, you can explore somewhere else, discover new weapons, experiment with different builds, and come back stronger. The game constantly rewards curiosity, and every corner of the Lands Between feels like it hides a secret worth discovering.

The combat is as satisfying as ever, with an insane amount of build variety, but the real highlight remains the boss encounters. Some fights are among FromSoftware’s best creations, combining spectacle, mechanics, and memorable moments.

Of course, the open-world structure is not perfect. Some areas and encounters feel less polished than others, and the amount of content can sometimes affect the overall pacing. But when Elden Ring reaches its peak, it delivers some of the greatest moments in modern game design.

After Dark Souls, Bloodborne and Sekiro, FromSoftware once again proved they know how to make players learn, adapt, and improve.

The first maybe 40 or so hours was some of the most fun I've ever had in any video game, and I realize I've been chasing that high ever since, and somehow it only got worse. 

Firstly, the most blatant weakness for me is the storytelling: it's a joke. I can tell there's some interesting lore and characters somewhere in there, but it's presented in a completely incomprehensible manner. 

"You must seek the Elden Ring and become Elden lord!" okay, cool. Why? You are given the vaguest of the vaguest motivations to do *anything* in this game. I meet random characters with absolutely no context or build-up, that apparently I'm supposed to care for.  I have no idea who am I fighting and why. There's barely any RP in this supposed RPG, as joining 'factions' and completing side-quests is completely inconsequential. Not to mention those aforementioned side-quests have incredibly obscure requirements to complete, some feel almost impossible without the wiki.

I understand FromSoft is known for indirect storytelling, but when you want to tell a classic, multilayered fantasy epic, this style simply does not work. It's a completely ridiculous proposition that I'm supposed to rely on vague item descriptions to understand major plot points. Again, this would be fine on some other game that wasn't heavily touted as "having a great narrative written by George RR Martin!!"

Once I realized the story was pretty much non-existent, my open world immersion and suspension of disbelief was irrecoverably shattered. I began to see cool ruins as nothing more than simple repeated 3D assets thrown randomly across the landscape. It's absolutely clear that the devs had no idea what the story behind most places in this game really was, they just expect the players to fill in the blanks. That is not even mentioning the INSANE amount of recycled areas, enemies and bosses in this game. 

Well, the story is kind of bad, at least the game can redeem itself with its gameplay right? Eh, sort of. Like I said in the beginning, I thoroughly enjoyed the early/midgame. The enemy variety was great, and I had tons of fun fighting the early bosses.

However, that's where much of my enjoyment ended. What I started realizing, is that the open world aspect of the game doesn't really work. Here's what happens in Elden Ring all the time: you stumble across a boss or a difficult area which feels way too hard and you think "okay, I'll just explore and come back later." You come back after some hours, realize you've grown vastly more powerful, and the fight becomes an unsatisfying cakewalk. It's such a shame too, because some of the coolest bosses visually were the exact ones I beat in one try. There were some bosses that I  didn't have to engage with, because I could just brute-force it by chugging down health potions. 

The other category of bosses and enemies is those that are wholly anti-fun, attacking so rapidly that you can't play in a proactive manner. There are bosses that legitimately feel like I was playing a turn-based game, since I could get in a hit safely once in a blue moon. There's so many cool skills and playstyles in this game, but it feels like you aren't allowed to experiment with any of them. My complaint has nothing to do with the difficulty, it's about the forced defensive and reactive playstyle.  

That is, if you don't use spirit summons, which are one of the most baffling design choices in this game. The spirits summons turn most fights into a joke, as they draw aggro from enemies and allow you to freely act as you wish. This is clearly meant to be an accessibility mechanic, but it almost feel like the devs designed certain encounters around them. It almost feels like the devs are constantly whispering my ears like "oh geez, this encounter sure is a bit difficult, are you sure you don't want to use the summons bro?"  

This all leads to an extremely unbalanced experience. If I died, it felt I got cheesed out. If I beat a difficult enemy, I felt I cheesed them, as opposed to feeling like a hero who has slain an epic monster. It all feels very...mechanical in nature, which is the absolute killer of my immersion.

Il gioco racconta di un universo incredibilmente complesso, con personaggi profondi, dalle storie intrecciate e legate in modo trascendentale al mondo. 
Ognuno dei quali immerso nell'ambiguità della dualità.
Elden ring racconta una storia "grigia", dove non esiste bene o male. Resta al giocatore l'approfondimento ed eventuale giudizio sulla moralità dei personaggi e le loro decisioni.

Il gioco fa vivere in ogni istante una narrazione quasi mitologica, supportata da uno stile artistico epico, capace di tradurre in colore, texture e geometria in eleganza, violenza, sofferenza e molto altro.

Il gameplay è lo scoglio che deve essere superato per godersi un universo infinito, in cui si respira arte da ogni frame.

- Beautiful open world
- Dark lore that you actually need to do a lot of exploration for 
- Challenging fights however the game has wide variety of weapons, spells and tools so there are plenty of solutions for difficult encounters as well as playstyles
- decent controls and UI (althrough it is noticable that the game was made for console)
- multiple endings
- fairly forgiving for Souls games

All in all, a really good game for adventure/RPG enjoyers.

**Elden Ring** is easily one of the best action RPGs I have ever played. From the moment I stepped into the Lands Between, I was amazed by the scale of the world, the freedom of exploration, and the incredible attention to detail. Every area feels unique, and there's always something new to discover, whether it's a hidden cave, a powerful boss, or valuable equipment.

What impressed me the most is the sense of exploration. The game rarely tells you exactly where to go, allowing you to explore at your own pace. Every time I wandered off the main path, I found interesting locations, secret dungeons, or challenging enemies. This constant feeling of discovery made every hour enjoyable and rewarding.

The combat system is another major highlight. Every weapon has its own moveset, and players can freely experiment with different builds, including melee, magic, faith, or hybrid playstyles. Boss fights are challenging but incredibly satisfying, requiring patience, observation, and practice rather than luck. Defeating a difficult boss after multiple attempts is one of the most rewarding experiences the game offers.

If I had to mention a small downside, it would be that the difficulty can be overwhelming for new players. Some bosses and areas require a lot of practice, and the game doesn't explain many mechanics in detail. However, I believe overcoming these challenges is also what makes Elden Ring so memorable.

Overall, Elden Ring is an outstanding masterpiece with breathtaking world design, deep combat mechanics, unforgettable boss battles, and an incredible sense of adventure. If you enjoy challenging action RPGs and open-world exploration, I highly recommend this game. It truly deserves all the praise it has received.


『ELDEN RING』は、私がこれまでプレイしたアクションRPGの中でも最高クラスの作品です。ゲームを始めてすぐに、その広大な世界、美しい景色、そして自由度の高い探索に強く引き込まれました。どのエリアにも個性があり、洞窟や遺跡、隠しアイテムや強敵など、探索するたびに新しい発見があります。

特に素晴らしいと感じたのは探索の楽しさです。ゲームはプレイヤーに細かく指示を出さず、自分の好きな順番で世界を冒険できます。道を少し外れるだけでも新しいダンジョンや装備、強敵に出会えるため、常に冒険している実感があります。

戦闘システムも非常に完成度が高く、武器や魔法、祈祷など多彩なビルドを自由に楽しめます。ボス戦は難易度こそ高いものの、敵の攻撃を覚え、少しずつ攻略していく過程は非常にやりがいがあります。何度も挑戦した末に勝利した時の達成感は、このゲームならではの魅力です。

唯一挙げるとすれば、初心者には難易度が高い点です。ゲーム内で詳しい説明が少なく、最初は戸惑うこともあります。しかし、その試行錯誤こそが『ELDEN RING』の面白さでもあると感じました。

総合的に見て、『ELDEN RING』は世界観、探索、戦闘、ボス戦のすべてが非常に高いレベルでまとまった傑作です。高難易度アクションやオープンワールドRPGが好きな人には、自信を持っておすすめできる作品です。


《艾爾登法環》是我玩過最優秀的動作角色扮演遊戲之一，也是一款讓人真正感受到探索樂趣的開放世界作品。從踏入交界地開始，廣闊的世界、壯觀的景色以及充滿神秘感的地圖，都讓我忍不住一直探索下去。幾乎每走一段路，都能發現新的地下城、隱藏道具或強大的 Boss，整個遊戲充滿驚喜。

我最喜歡的是遊戲高度自由的探索方式。它不會一直要求玩家照著固定路線前進，而是讓玩家自由決定冒險方向。就算偏離主線，也經常能找到新的裝備、支線任務或特殊地點，因此每一次探索都很有價值，也讓人願意花很多時間仔細探索整張地圖。

戰鬥系統也是本作最大的亮點之一。遊戲提供大量武器、戰技、魔法與禱告，可以自由搭配出各種不同的流派。每場 Boss 戰都需要觀察敵人的攻擊節奏，學會閃避與反擊，而不是單純依靠裝備數值。雖然難度不低，但成功擊敗強敵後，那種成就感是其他遊戲很難帶來的。

如果要說缺點，我認為最大的挑戰就是對新玩家比較不友善。部分 Boss 難度非常高，遊戲也不會詳細教學所有系統，因此剛開始可能需要花不少時間適應。不過，只要慢慢熟悉遊戲機制，就會越來越享受整個冒險過程。

整體而言，《艾爾登法環》是一款完成度極高的作品。無論是世界觀、美術設計、探索自由度、戰鬥系統還是 Boss 設計，都展現出極高的水準。如果你喜歡具有挑戰性的動作 RPG 與開放世界冒險，我非常推薦這款遊戲，它絕對值得投入數十甚至數百個小時去體驗。

Вероятно, одна из лучших игр. Я готов защищать Elden Ring, даже не смотря на то, что сам порой сильно срываюсь и говорю что игра плохая. 
[hr][/hr]
[h1]Открытый мир[/h1]
Пожалуй, самая частая причина хейта игры. Да, в игре есть огромный открытый мир, полный кучи расходников или материалов для создания, будем честны, не сильно вам полезными. Но большие открытые пространства, сцены сражений или пустые хижины это буквально последствия раскола. 
[spoiler]Пустые вершины великанов, Засыпанный пеплом Лейнделл а так же заражённые Звёздные пустоши[/spoiler] - всё это часть лора игры. Да, мир выглядит "пустым", но в игре даётся быстрое перемещение между благодатями а также конь, на котором можно быстро пробежать локации. В итоге, я считаю, что открытый мир прекрасно передаёт атмосферу и настроение Elden Ring
[hr][/hr]
[h1]Сюжет и Лор[/h1]
игра не даёт прямых ответов на сюжетные вопросы, не говорит прямо о тех или иных событиях. Игра представляет возможность самим построить теории и догадки. Сюда же можно и приплести квестовые линии, которые, на самом деле мало понятны. Часто ты будешь случайно натыкаться на персонажей, нужных для продвижения квеста. Но такая загадочность наоборот играет на руку. Ты смотришь описания предметов, рассматриваешь локации и разборы лора на ютубе. Я считаю что лор в этой игре просто гениален. Одним словом, ты будто оживший герой какой фентезийной истории, написанной Джордж Р. Р. Мартином. 
[hr][/hr] 
[h1]Боевка и Боссы[/h1] 
Это лучшая часть игры. Тут более 100 боссов, куча врагов, и у каждого из них свой лор и особенности, специальные атаки. Что уж говорить, если только сюжетные боссы настолько разные. Сражение с каждым из них - это боевой танец, в котором ты сражаешься лицом к лицу с богами. То, насколько игра прекрасна, говорит о том, какие здесь красивые локации и боссы. О визуале в этой игре можно говорить вечно. И да, они сложные, но это не значит, что ты должен страдать. Отличие этого жанра в том, что у тебя полностью развязаны руки. Ты можешь использовать любое оружие, любую броню, талисманы и баффы. Ты можешь составить абсолютно любой билд под слабости босса, изучив его мув-сет и низкую сопротивляемость. Одним словом, игра не заставляет тебя страдать, она даёт тебе огромный открытый мир для изучения не просто так.  [spoiler]У малении слабый баланс и низкое сопротивление к кровотоку,  а Двое из божественной кожи имеют плохое сопротивление ко сну[/spoiler] . Ещё важно забыть все эти мнения что тот или иной билд неправильный: казуальный, перекачанный или неинтересный. Просто забейте и играйте в свою игру. Призовите фантомов на бесячего босса, попробуйте магический билд или билд в силу, самое главное - кайфаните.
[hr][/hr]  
[h1]Заключение[/h1] 
Эта игра прекрасна. Тут тысячи возможностей билда и невероятно красивый открытый мир. Чего уж говорить о реиграбельности, ведь игра предоставляет прохождения NG+, в которых ты, полностью прокачанный идёшь перепроходить игру со своим уровнем и снаряжением. Можно создавать челленджи или разные сохранения с разными целями: только маг оружия, только гравитационная магия или, скажем, только сила. игра однозначно 10/10, S тир. Стоит своих денег

This game was incredibly disappointing to play.
For starters, this game is absolutely beautiful. The set pieces, the enemies, the backgrounds, the game is gorgeous to an unbelievable degree. What I find a bit lacking, however, is that a lot of the enemies and levels can feel overdesigned and clunky to a degree where the deeper thoughts of the design are unreadable. While high gothic architecture is always appreciated, it can definitely feel eye glazing at times when the developers obviously didn't care as much about a location as others. The biggest problems I found with this being the numerous catacombs, caves, forts, and mines that are present throughout the game. Although they are at numerous locations, with very distinct landscapes, there's never anything visually interesting about them that wasn't done before. It makes it feel very video-gamey and copy and paste, when I felt that the worldbuilding of this game was incredibly interesting originally.

The difficulty of the game is far higher than previous souls titles, which in itself is not bad. However, there is a clear distinction between boss encounters. There's Margit, who feel very intentionally designed, while remaining difficult in a fair way, maintaining the "I died, what did I do wrong" mindset that many of the previous games seem to hold. Then there's Knight Ordovis, which is a boss encounter stapling two mini-bosses you have already fought, then taking to precautions to make it feel like a well-made duo boss. The first knight will always cover the second's punish windows, and if you're unlucky, they will attack at such intervals where it is impossible to not take damage. The vast majority of this game is a good boss fight, followed by 2 or 3 boring to bad ones (Some of these being repeat bosses that you have already fought plenty of times before). The difficulty, then, feels less like a natural result of the game attempting to challenge you in an interesting way, but devolves into feeling like it is overly punishing and unfair because they didn't take the extra second to ensure the encounter played smoothly. It doesn't help that your rune gain is decreased if you summon additional players, so it makes single bosses crammed into a duo fight feel even worse, since you are discouraged to summon others to help even the fight out (See gargoyles and godskin duo). 

The game itself and its grandness seems impressive at first, since the selling point of over 100 bosses appears incredible, but you soon realize that the game only has over 100 boss encounters because of how much they reuse and repurpose the same enemy over and over again. I personally would have preferred a smaller world, if it meant having less repeat encounters, but the game insists on reusing things that don't make sense. For example, the tree sentinel being a returning encounter makes sense. But having an Ancient Hero of Zamor be in a catacomb makes it feel very repetitive. Why is the boss here? Because you reached the end of the dungeon. Erdtree Avatars guarding the Minor Erdtrees makes sense. Having a named magma wyrm followed by a nameless magma wyrm in another unrelated cave is boring and repetitive. Ancient Dragon Lansseax was extremely cool to find, but now, one of the later game areas throws an identical copy of the fight, thus making it less impactful. The critique here is not that the individual encounter was bad, it's moreso that the individual encounter's overall effect and impact in the game is weakened since now there are just more enemies that act exactly like the boss.

I would suggest playing this game with an open mind and a guide. Playing guideless will cause you to miss many things that the game, and most players, would deem as "important" and "required." Do not be surprised if the open world leads you to having a weapon lacking upgrades for where you're supposed to be. Perhaps, had I started the game with a guide in hand, I would not have struggled as much, but I also deem myself to be a pretty experienced souls-like player and have always enjoyed the problem solving and natural progression of the game. Sadly, it seems that this game tried to be too big, but didn't have enough things to fill the huge map.

Elden Ring isn't just a masterpiece. It's the gold standard for open-world RPGs.

The Lands Between is breathtaking, filled with secrets, unforgettable locations, and endless reasons to explore. Every cave, castle, and hidden path rewards your curiosity instead of wasting your time.

The soundtrack, art direction, lore, and world design are second to none. Instead of holding your hand, Elden Ring lets you discover its world at your own pace, making every major discovery feel genuinely rewarding.

Even after hundreds of hours, I'm still finding new weapons, hidden areas, quests, and bosses. Very few games can keep that sense of wonder alive for so long.

A once-in-a-generation masterpiece and easily one of the greatest games ever created.

Elden Ring is a fascinating evolution of the Souls formula. I was skeptical about moving the series into a fully open world, but it worked much better than I expected.

The game offers an incredible amount of freedom. You can experiment with countless character builds, approach challenges in different ways, and explore a massive world filled with interesting locations, deep lore, and a huge variety of enemies. Some boss fights are genuinely memorable, although others suffer from extremely delayed animations that can make fights feel less satisfying than they should.

The open world design is both the game's biggest strength and its biggest weakness. Compared to the more focused structure of Dark Souls or Bloodborne, Elden Ring sometimes feels a little too stretched out. Many caves, catacombs, and smaller dungeons start to feel repetitive after a while, with similar layouts and rewards.

The quality of exploration also decreases in later parts of the game. The Mountaintops of the Giants especially show that a bigger world does not always mean a better one, as this area feels much less interesting compared to the earlier regions.

Despite these issues, Elden Ring is still a very enjoyable action RPG with a unique atmosphere, great combat, and a huge amount of freedom. It successfully brings the Souls formula into an open world, even if some parts of the experience feel less polished compared to FromSoftware's more focused games.

Pros:

+ Huge variety of character builds
+ Interesting lore and world building
+ Many memorable enemies and locations
+ Great combat system
+ Lots of exploration

Cons:

- Some bosses rely too much on delayed attacks
- Many caves and catacombs feel too similar
- The open world can feel less focused than previous Souls games
- Later areas are weaker

This review is NOT how I would rate the game. If it was, I'd give it a 11/10. Great gameplay, story, art, everything! This review is if I would recommend this game to other people who are looking through Elden Ring steam reviews, and If you aren't sure on whether to get this game or not, please listen to what I have to say.

If you are looking for a game with amazing... Everything... get this game. It is allows thousands of different playstyles with thousands of great weapons and armor. Even better with the DLC! HOWEVER... this game does not hold your hand whatsoever, and that is partially why I don't recommend it to newer souls players or people who want to have a laid back time. Before you flame me or tell me I'm wrong, I beat the game with 120 hours with no guide or help whatsoever, so although some things might be wrong, I have a good amount of experience with this game. Regarding this "hand holding" issue, I have two major concerns. 

1. This game is extremely vague with where you are supposed to go.
Sights of Graces are helpful and tell you where to be to some extent, but in some instances, it doesn't help you outright and you are forced to look up where to go or what to do. There is a great example around 1/4-1/3 of the way into the game that I constantly find people looking up where to go.

2. Quest and Items can be extremely hard to find and are locked behind dialogue options, choices, bosses killed etc. Which gets rid of the desire to pursue it in the first place.
This kinda goes with my first reason, but this is such a large issue that it should be mentioned. All of my friends who have played this game struggled to level up or find items, which led them to look up where to go, defeating basically the entire purpose of this game of discovery. I know this game is supposed to be extremely difficult, (I have played other fromsoftware games like sekiro) but for a game as large and expansive as Elden ring, I feel that there should be some sort of way to at least track quests or give you a hint of where to go.

In conclusion, if you skipped everything else, If you are a die hard FromSoftware fan 100% get this game, it is peak. But if you are not familiar with how FromSoftware does it, Elden Ring should not be the first game you play. It overwhelms many beginners and causes them to quit early.
